skill.name: socialmedia-gpthalf
skill.description: Review public posts, pasted text, and local images for AI-origin evidence. The skill separates image credentials, Simplified Chinese writing patterns, and estimated reader reactions.
skill.summary: Review AI-origin evidence, Chinese writing patterns, and likely reader reactions in public posts.
skill.author: yuzhang-zhong

security_audit.summary: Most flags are documentation, data validation, or report formatting, and no evidence of author-planted prompt injection was found. The optional Hive integration uploads selected images and does not disable redirects. Separate findings cover a media consent gap, unsafe Markdown rendering, and uncorroborated disclosures presented as verified.

remediation.issue: Hive upload redirects are not disabled.
remediation.suggestion: Disable upload redirects and reject unexpected destinations before sending image bytes. Show the destination and selected assets during consent.

remediation.issue: Image validation and use open the media path separately.
remediation.suggestion: Validate and hash a private immutable copy. Use that same copy for C2PA analysis and any approved upload.

remediation.issue: Untrusted text can become active Markdown.
remediation.suggestion: Escape untrusted strings before Markdown interpolation. Disable raw HTML and remote embeds in rendered reports.

remediation.issue: Case observations can produce verified provenance without source corroboration.
remediation.suggestion: Label case observations as reported until a trusted capture confirms the exact label or disclosure on the scoped asset.

semantic_findings.title: Image Consent Is Not Bound to the Uploaded Bytes
semantic_findings.description: The CLI rechecks the selected image but the provider later reopens its path. A file changed between those operations can invalidate the consent record.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The validation result contains metadata, not an open handle. The provider opens the path independently, so the uploaded bytes are not rechecked against the recorded digest.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Excerpts Are Rendered as Markdown
semantic_findings.description: Report excerpts and reception text are inserted without Markdown escaping. A viewer that permits remote embeds or raw HTML can display deceptive content or initiate network requests.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The formatter directly interpolates source-derived excerpts and reception strings into the saved Markdown. Effects depend on the downstream viewer.

semantic_findings.title: Uncorroborated Disclosures Are Marked Verified
semantic_findings.description: A claim in a supplied case can be labeled verified with high confidence without independent confirmation that the platform or author made it.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The CLI validates the observation fields, and the evidence policy matches disclosure wording. Neither step authenticates the source before granting the verified verdict.

content.user_title: Assess AI-Origin Evidence in Social Posts
content.value_statement: Formulaic writing and missing image credentials can lead to incorrect claims about AI use. This skill reports source evidence, writing patterns, and possible reader reactions separately.
actual_capabilities: Review pasted text, local images, or visible public post content when a browser is available.
Check local images for C2PA Content Credentials and distinguish generative edits from full generation.
Highlight sentence-level patterns and report document-level writing signals for Simplified Chinese.
Estimate supportive, neutral, and skeptical reader reactions using excerpts or visible page evidence.
Run optional Hive image analysis only for explicitly selected images after permission.
Produce Markdown and structured JSON reports that separate evidence, coverage, and uncertainty.
limitations: Local text rules are uncalibrated and support Simplified Chinese only. Short samples may provide too little evidence.
Style matches, detector signals, and missing credentials do not prove whether a person used AI.
Reader reactions are estimates, not results from real audience testing.
Public pages may be inaccessible. Local credential checks require the C2PA library, and Hive checks require permission and a configured key.

use_cases.title: Check an Image Disclosure
use_cases.description: Compare an original image's credentials with the disclosure visible on a public post. Keep any conclusion specific to the inspected image.

use_cases.title: Review Chinese Writing Patterns
use_cases.description: Find repetitive phrasing in a public Simplified Chinese post and consider how its genre could explain those patterns.

use_cases.title: Compare Reader Perspectives
use_cases.description: Estimate how supportive, neutral, and skeptical readers might respond to a public announcement. Use excerpts to explain likely confusion or mistrust.

prompt_templates.title: Check Pasted Text
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pasted Simplified Chinese post locally. Point out any repeated wording and tell me whether the sample is long enough to assess: [post text].

prompt_templates.title: Inspect One Original Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the attached original image for Content Credentials. Distinguish generative editing from full generation, report any missing evidence, and do not upload the image.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Reader Perspectives
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: a public post with text and media
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [public post URL] from supportive, neutral, and skeptical perspectives before checking AI-origin evidence. Cite visible details for each reaction and state what you could not access.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Multi-Image Post
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: asset-level evidence and optional processing
prompt_templates.prompt: For [post text and original images], create an asset-by-asset report. Separate disclosures, credentials, text patterns, and reader reactions. Ask for permission before sending any specific image to Hive.

output_examples.input: An original PNG from a public post, with external processing disabled.
output_examples.output: No usable Content Credentials were found in this image. Hive was not called. The origin remains undetermined.

output_examples.input: A long Simplified Chinese launch announcement with repeated transitions.
output: Similar transitions recur across several paragraphs. This is a writing pattern, not proof of AI use.
A skeptical reader may find the repeated benefits vague because the post gives no specific examples.

best_practices: Provide original image files, and record whether each disclosure applies to text, an image, or the whole post.
Keep external processing off unless you have permission to send the specific image to Hive.
Confirm consequential conclusions with original files, observable disclosures, or other independent evidence.
anti_patterns: Treating formulaic language, a detector output, or missing credentials as conclusive proof of authorship.
Applying a finding about one image to the whole post, account, or author.
Using estimated reader reactions as survey results or as evidence of AI use.

faq.question: Does this skill tell me who wrote a post?
faq.answer: No. It separates available provenance, detector signals, and writing patterns. It does not identify the author or provide an AI percentage.

faq.question: Does local pattern analysis support English?
faq.answer: The bundled text rules are designed for Simplified Chinese. Other languages can still receive a reader review or separate image checks.

faq.question: Does the analyzer send my text to a detector?
faq.answer: No. The Python analyzer checks text locally. Only explicitly approved image selections are eligible for the optional Hive upload.

faq.question: What does missing C2PA metadata mean?
faq.answer: There are no usable Content Credentials from that check. This does not establish whether the image was made by a person or with AI.

faq.question: What if the public link is inaccessible?
faq.answer: Provide the visible post text or attach the original media. The review should state which context it could not inspect.

faq.question: Are the reader reactions measured?
faq.answer: No. The three reactions are estimates based on the post and its visible context. Use real reader testing for important decisions.
